label: Cisco Catalyst 1000 C1000-48P-4G-L
description: Cisco Catalyst 1000 C1000-48P-4G-L - 48x 1G RJ-45 all PoE+ (802.3af/at, 30 W a port, 370 W budget), 4x 1G SFP uplink cages, 104 Gbps switching bandwidth, 77.38 Mpps at 64 bytes, fan-cooled 1U Cisco IOS L2 access switch.

poe.note: 370 W PoE budget across 48 PoE+ ports, IEEE 802.3af/802.3at PSE, 30 W maximum a port. Perpetual PoE holds power on the PD across a reload. The budget, not the port count, is the ceiling: 24 Class-3 (15.4 W) PDs or 12 30 W PDs fit (24 x 15.4 W = 369.6 W, 12 x 30 W = 360 W).

notes: Datasheet Table 1 and Table 2: 48 copper ports, 4x 1G SFP uplink cages, 370 W PoE budget, one fan, 36.1 dB sound pressure, 17.48 x 13.78 x 1.73 in deep, 5.43 kg; single internal autoranging 100-240 VAC supply; 77.38 Mpps forwarding rate; 16,000 unicast MAC entries, 256 active VLANs, 4094 VLAN IDs, 64 STP instances, 9198-byte L3 MTU, 10,240-byte jumbo frame. The switching bandwidth is the sum of every port at line rate, so no port group is oversubscribed. RJ-45 console (EIA/TIA-232) at 9600 baud, 8 data bits, 1 stop bit, no parity, no flow control; a USB Type A port takes a FAT-formatted flash drive for image and configuration recovery. Cisco calls the series Layer 2, but Table 2 budgets 542 IPv4 direct and 256 indirect routes (414/128 for IPv6), so static inter-VLAN routing is modelled as l3-forward, not a full L3 feature set. No 802.3bt anywhere in the series: 30 W a port is the ceiling. Discrepancy: the 24/48-port Hardware Installation Guide model table describes the 48P-4G-L as 48 ports with 12 PoE+ ports (370 W budget) and 36 Ethernet ports, while the datasheet configuration and ordering tables both give 48 PoE+ ports at 370 W, and the 15.2(7)E release notes agree with the datasheet. 48 PoE+ ports is modelled; the HIG line is the outlier and reads like the 48PP-4G-L (12 PoE+ ports, 180 W), a different SKU.
